_meta.purpose: Registry of every job source the pipeline is permitted to call.
_meta.compliance_rule: Build spec Rule 2. LinkedIn, Indeed and Glassdoor are NOT here and must never be added - their terms prohibit automated collection. Only official/public APIs and employer-published feeds are listed. Any source without a legitimate API is recorded under manual_review_only and is never fetched programmatically.
_meta.provenance_rule: Every board token below returned HTTP 200 with a non-empty job list when probed on 2026-08-08. Nothing in this file is a guess. Re-run `python -m jobfinder.phase2.verify_sources` to re-probe; dead tokens are marked, never silently dropped.

etiquette.note: One identified caller, rate-limited, no concurrency against a single host. These are free public endpoints and the pipeline should not cost their operators anything noticeable.

aggregators.name: remoteok
aggregators.salary_note: RemoteOK exposes salary_min/salary_max but frequently returns 0 or omits them. A 0 is treated as NOT DISCLOSED, never as a salary of zero.
aggregators.first_record_note: Index 0 of the RemoteOK array is an API legal/attribution notice, not a job. It must be skipped or it becomes a phantom posting.

aggregators.name: arbeitnow
aggregators.coverage: Europe, Germany-weighted. Tags frequently include visa-sponsorship signals, which is directly useful for a candidate who needs sponsorship everywhere.
aggregators.salary_note: No structured salary field. Salary is therefore always stored as not disclosed for this source unless a range is parsed out of the description text, in which case it is stored with salary_source='parsed_from_description' and flagged lower-confidence.

aggregators.name: himalayas
aggregators.terms: Read at himalayas.app/api on 2026-09-25: free public JSON API, no auth. Conditions: link back to the Himalayas URL and name Himalayas as the source; do not resubmit its jobs to other boards (Jooble, Google Jobs, LinkedIn...); data refreshes daily so polling more than daily brings nothing. Career Scout stores and shows the link-back URL, republishes nothing, and runs once a day.
aggregators.enabled_by: T031b (2026-09-25) — the deliberate decision the earlier note asked for.

aggregators.name: jobicy
aggregators.terms: The API's own friendlyNotice (2026-09-25): credit Jobicy with a direct link to the source, and send applications to the original job URL in the feed. Career Scout stores that URL as the posting's source and apply target.
aggregators.enabled_by: T031b (2026-09-25) — the deliberate decision the earlier note asked for.

greenhouse.content_note: The `content` field is HTML-escaped HTML. It must be unescaped and stripped before any keyword matching, or skill matching silently fails on entities like <p>.

rejected_tokens.reason: Returns 388 postings but is Lever's own demo/sandbox board, not a real employer. Ingesting it would inject fake jobs into a system whose entire premise is that no fabricated data enters it.
HTTP 404 - not hosted on Lever. Removed rather than left in as a plausible-looking dead token.

government_portals.name: usajobs
government_portals.auth_note: Requires a free API key plus a User-Agent email, requested at https://developer.usajobs.gov/APIRequest. NOT ENABLED because no key has been supplied - see docs/CREDENTIALS.md. This is a stop-and-ask item, not something to stub.
government_portals.relevance: US federal roles. Note these are overwhelmingly restricted to US citizens, so relevance to this candidate is low even once enabled.

government_portals.name: eures
government_portals.auth_note: The EU EURES portal does not currently expose a documented stable public JSON API for third-party job search. Left disabled rather than scraped - Rule 2 says skip and log, not scrape.
